subject.title: fix(google-meet): recover_current_tab without a url no longer attaches to unrelated Meet tabs

question: Should URL-less Google Meet recovery permanently fail closed when the calling runtime has no owned tab, requiring an explicit URL instead of preserving the prior arbitrary-tab fallback?
rationale: The patch correctly removes a path that can focus and grant microphone/camera permissions to another session’s tab, but it also changes the behavior of existing URL-less callers that may have depended on broad tab discovery.

options.title: Adopt scoped recovery
options.body: Merge the session-owned-only behavior and require an explicit URL when no owned target exists, prioritizing browser-tab ownership over legacy broad recovery.

options.title: Preserve legacy fallback
options.body: Keep arbitrary-tab recovery as an explicit opt-in compatibility mode, accepting that it cannot provide the same ownership protection by default.

recommendation.title: Adopt scoped recovery
recommendation.body: Merge the session-owned-only behavior and require an explicit URL when no owned target exists, prioritizing browser-tab ownership over legacy broad recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership could not be attributed reliably from the supplied history, so the decision should route to the Google Meet/plugin area owner.
